4. Mr. Mustafizur Rahman Khan, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner, at the very outset, submits that the Adalat acted illegality in restoring the execution case under section 57 of the Ain since there is a specific provision of special law of limitation in the statute. The learned advocate further submits that since the execution case was filed in the year 2004 and was subsequently rejected for default in the year 2011 for the laches of the decree-holder bank, it had been left with an option to file a new execution case under the provision of sub-section (4) of section 28 of the Ain. But restoration of an execution case, which apparently was barred by special law of limitation, was completely without jurisdiction. 

 6. Mr. Md. Hefzul Bari, learned advocate for the respondent-Bank having drawn our attention to section 48 of the Ain submits that for the purpose of reckoning the period of limitation the days counted should be the working days only. According to the learned Advocate, 6 (six) years’ time had not been elapsed from the date of filing of the Execution Case, when the same was rejected for default on 19.06.2011 and therefore, the submission of the learned advocate for the petitioner about law of limitation has no merit. 

 "Section 28(1) The Limitation Act, 19 এ The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 এ ভিন্নতর যে বিধান থাকুক না কেন, ডিক্রীদার, আদালতযোগে ডিক্রী বা আদেশ কায্যকর করিতে ইচ্ছা করিলে, ডিক্রী বা আদেশ প্রদত্ত হওয়ার অনূর্ধ্ব ১(এক) বৎসরের মধ্যে, ধারা ২৯ এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে জারীর জন্য আদালতে দরখাস্ত দাখিল করিয়া মামলা করিবে। 

 From a close reading of the above quoted text, it appears that sub-section (1) of section 28 has imposed a restriction on the decree-holder that the execution case shall have to be filed within I (one) year from the date of passing a decree subject to the provision of section 29 of the Ain. Sub-section (3) there of speaks about filing of second or subsequent execution case fixing a time limit of 1(one) year from the date of rejection or disposal of the first execution case. Sub-section(4) creates an embargo upon the decree-holder providing the legal consequence that the new execution case shall be rejected summarily if it is filed after expiry of the period of 6(six) years from the date of filing of the first execution case. In the instant case, execution case was filed on 08.03.2004 pursuant to the judgment and decree dated 02.11.2003 and at one stage of the proceedings the execution case was dismissed for default (তৎবিরের অভাবে খারিজ) on 19.06.2011 i.e. after expiry of 6 (six) years. Having considered an application for restoration, at the instance of the decree-holder bank, it was restored to its original file and number by order dated 05.07.2011 on taking recourse of section 57 of the Ain. When the statute prescribes the special provision of limitation for filing a new Artha Rin Execution Case after rejection (খারিজ) or disposal (নিস্পত্তি) of the first execution case, taking shelter of the inherent jurisdiction under section 57 of the Ain for restoration of the same will defeat the whole purpose of special law of limitation as contemplated in the statute. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the related special law of limitation, we are constrained to hold that the restoration of execution case under section 57 of the Ain should be declared to have been done without lawful authority. Moreover, the inherent power of the court cannot be invoked to enable the Court to break through the clear provision of the law of limitation. Similarly, the inherent jurisdiction cannot be exercised so as to conflict with a statute or statutory provision framed for a particular purpose. In the instant case, when the filing of a new execution case under the statutory provision of section 28(4) had been barred by the special law of limitation, the decree-holder taking technical resort achieved the goal which is not allowed under the law. Despite the statutory provision of special law of limitation if the decree-holder is allowed to resort inherent jurisdiction of the court for ventilate his grievances, the purpose of the special law of limitation as contemplated in section 28 of the Ain will become meaningless and the execution case will never be ended. The right of the decree-holder in accordance with the statute has apparently extinguished as a legal consequence of special provision of limitation incorporated therein. With regard to the submission of the learned advocate for the respondent no.2 Bank, about section 48 of the Ain, we hold that the provision of section 48 of the Ain will not create any bar or hindrance for the purpose of reckoning 6(six) years of time as a calendar 6 (six) years as contemplated in sub-section (4) of section 28 of the Ain. Moreover, the provision of special law of limitation under section 28 of the Ain is not depended upon section 48 of the statute.
